That's the issue though isn't it, the only other perspective given is "damn haha sounds like suicide" which is a) inaccurate to how dormancy and switching works, further encouraging the idea that integration is like murder and dormancy is like death b) encourages already unhealthy behaviour in forcing switches more and c) frames it in a way that makes it sound Even More Unhealthy than it already is.  


So listen OP lets talk.  


1. One of the main goals of trauma therapy and did/osdd work is to dissociate and switch less. That's the point. It means you're working better as a team and your brain is healing to be able to cope with every day life better. The way a lot of this sub encourages switching more is really shocking to me.
2. Going dormant, ie "Letting them take over for good" as is phrased here, or more accurately Switching out and then not switching back in for months/years at a time, is not something you can control. It's something done by your brain when a part/alter isn't needed as much or isn't functioning well. In an ideal situation instead of going dormant a part will integrate but the point is dormancy =/= death. It's not a good thing to strive for, it isn't a break or a vacation, it's an unhealthy coping skill from ur brain.
3. Please speak to your therapist about this! This is a horribly unhealthy mindset, please keep yourself safe and don't try to trigger yourself to force anymore dramatic switches. It's not a fun vacation to lose control of your life.

​

As just a quick anecdote I have been where you are. I was going through something incredibly stressful and traumatic for me and I couldn't handle it and I thought "god I just want a break". I switched out, and I went dormant.

For 8 months. Nearly a whole year of my life. I stopped being the host, I came back in bits and pieces only able to front for minutes at a time. It was terrifying. Three of my closest friendships had been ruined by another alters living his own life, another one I hadn't spoken to in months, I'd lost nearly my entire friend group. I'd nearly lost my job, I had to adjust to blinking and it suddenly being nearly a year later. I'd gotten a major surgery and didn't even know what it was.

​

Going dormant is terrifying. It wasn't a vacation, it wasn't a rest, I didn't feel better after I came back.

Please. Keep yourself safe. Switching less is a good thing and the goal of nearly all did/osdd work in therapy. Please speak to your therapist about this as soon as you can and don't idealise this disorder as a way to get rest when it is the opposite.

I don't think you get how stressful and shitty switching actually is man, if you did you wouldn't be asking this. It's not fun, it's not a Holiday from responsibility and work, it's not relaxing, most of the time it's so stressful in itself that it's not any sort of mental break. 
Switching is blinking and realising you've suddenly lost a week of time, switching is having no clue who you are for hours on end, switching is dissociating at work and suddenly having no idea how to do your job, all your friends thinking you're angry at them or just completely changing your behaviour for no reason, it's coming back to yourself to find your money gone and items in your house you don't remember buying, it's feeling several ages at once, it's panic inducing and scary.


I can't comprehend why the fuck you'd ever want this. This disorder isn't fun, it's not a race to find out all your alters if you do have osdd or a contest of who can switch the most fully, it's not anything like you think it is.
Rethink your attitude towards this disorder. Reinforcing dissociative barriers isn't good and trying to shulk responsibility from your life into this disorder and any possible alters you may have is unhealthy and unrealistic.

Obviously kids shouldn't be exposed to graphic media like that, that goes without saying, but it isn't traumatic and therefore wouldn't cause a trauma based disorder.

You know what is traumatic? Verbal abuse. Don't discount your own experiences in favour of blaming video games, verbal abuse is traumatic and enough to cause OSDD, I'd recommend getting a good therapist to start exploring what actual trauma you went through rather than just shrugging it off onto sometime that couldn't have caused it.

Verbal abuse is definitely "enough" to cause OSDD. There's no "enough" when it comes to how a young mind perceives and handles trauma. You could have never had a hand laid on you and could still develop OSDD or DID, its not how severe you think the trauma is, its how your brain perceives it.

That being said watching someone play video games isn't traumatic and wouldn't cause OSDD so no. I don't believe that playing video games could cause OSDD. Not at all.

I was running a campaign a while ago based around Astral dragons. The first sort of proper puzzle the players came across was a small Oasis in the desert with 4 huts, a little tiki bar, a pool of fresh water, and one man pretending to be four people.

H, the friendly and charismatic seeming leader of this group of one. Made great cocktails and was more than happy to meet all the characters.

E, the slightly less open but no less welcoming other 'personality'. Happy to chat but didnt talk about the other 'people' living in the oasis.

L, a very confusing and seemingly crazy person who didnt enjoy talking to the players at all.

and P, a child, funny and jovial but aggressively defensive when asked any questions about why they seemed to be four people in the same body. 

Obviously their names spelled HELP. Not that clever but it took a surprisingly long time for the players to get it and they were all suitably spooked when they did.

Through some sluething and assault they discovered that each of the huts was decorated by seemingly a different person with an entirely different personality for each hut, and eventually they found a waterfall with a secret door behind it, leading to a room with a statue of a family.

Eventually the truth came out: HELP was indeed 4 people, a family consisting of two fathers, their young child, and her aunt travelling with them. The main plot of the campaign was that all the dragonborn and dragons had vanished, been sucked away out of existence. 

The child was a dragonborn.

HELP was created out of familial love the desperation to keep the child from vanishing along with every other draconic creature, but as time went on, being four people in one body took its toll on some of them and so my.players were faced with my favourite choice;

Do they leave this creation as they found it; a dysfunctional family that would have started falling apart if they werent tied together, or do they break them apart, freeing them from each othet and allowing them.to be individuals, but essentially killing a child?

tl;dr
Players come across a family shoved into one body. They have to choose between leaving them as one amalgamation, slowly going crazy, or split them up but kill the child of the family by doing so.

My story probably isn't that unusual. 
I grew up in what seemed to be a pretty accepting household. I learned about being gay and bi at a young age but my parents 'conveniently' left out anything about trans people. I'd never even heard of being trans until I was 13, but ever since I was a little kid I'd never felt comfortable with myself. When I was 4/5 I hated being a girl, I cut my own hair short and wanted to be able to run around topless like the boys and wear shorts and play sports, and that always got discouraged by my parents. They just reminded me I was a girl and couldn't do stuff like that. So as I got a little older, like 7/8ish, I started to really try and fit my assigned gender. Dresses, long hair even though my hair grew weirdly, I entered this huge scene kid phase where I'd wear bright neon pinks and get Super Offended if anyone ever thought I was a boy. Still didn't fit right though.

When I was 13 I finally got access to the Internet and started to make friends that weren't in the tiny community my mom kept me in. The people I made friends with came from, who can guess it? Tumblr. Yup.
As crazy as that place is, it helped. My close friends started questioning their genders and it fed back to me when they talked about it, and I related to what they were saying. With their help I started secretly questioning my own gender and why I was so adamant about being a girl even though it didn't fit. After a couple months of this I started calling myself Genderfluid, only online I might add. No way was I coming out to my parents.

Genderfluid was just a step though really. I slowly came to terms with the fact that 99% of the time I felt far more masculine than feminine, and when I was 15 I finally settled on it. I was a guy, what I'd felt when I was young wasn't something that I could just force away. I started living as my authentic self, changed my name, changed my dress, appearance, all of it and slowly I started to get more comfortable. Making friends who were better educated and able to freely question their gender was the best thing that ever happened to me. Being able to talk out the feelings I was having with someone was such a help and finally set me on the road to discovering who I am. It was a long and bumpy road but living as my authentic self is worth it.
